v.why: Replacing a missing direct edge with a conv adds a new path and gains more than swapping one existing op for another.
Edge 0 feeds node 1, so replacing none with a conv restores connectivity and gains more than replacing an existing op.
Going from no edge to a 3x3 conv on a path into the output is a bigger improvement than conv replacing another op.
Skip replacing none adds a useful path, while skip replacing a conv typically loses accuracy.
Removing edge 0 while edge 1 is already none cuts the input off from the output, collapsing accuracy.
Removing a 3x3 conv on the direct edge loses more than removing a pool or skip.
With the direct edge 3 absent, removing edge 5 eliminates more of the routes into the output.
With edge 0 absent, node 1 is unreachable and edge 2 is dead, so the edit has little effect.
Edge 4 starts at node 1, which is unreachable when edge 0 is none, so its conv does nothing.
Adding a direct skip from input to output where none existed improves gradient flow and accuracy more than replacing an existing op.
